answer.rationale: Current conditions show simultaneous decline in activation (6% QoQ) and onboarding completion (4% QoQ). Memory 91 demonstrates that in-product activation messaging improved week-one engagement and nudged accounts to first meaningful action. Memory 86 shows onboarding streamlining lifted adoption. Since we have capacity for one experiment and activation decline is the more acute metric, we should verify the activation_messaging approach (memory_91) which produced engagement lift without retention risk. We also verify memory_86 to confirm onboarding simplification remains valid as a reference point. Activation_messaging is preferred over promotional_pricing because memory_73 warns that aggressive SMB discounts damage renewal (retention -12%), which contradicts our primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue. A standard_experiment scale balances learning velocity against risk, and allows us to preserve uncertainty about whether activation messaging will work equivalently well at current competitive conditions.
